Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Magelang Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.

4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Governmental Affairs that are the authority of the Region.

6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

7. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of physical and verbal means that poses a danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.

11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.

12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 13. Victims of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic losses, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including victims are their heirs.

14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.

15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for trafficking in persons in

Magelang Regency.

16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.

17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the work environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.

19. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and socially.

20. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.

21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

23. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3

The objectives of protecting women and children from acts of violence and discrimination are to:

a. prevent acts of violence and discrimination against women and children including trafficking in persons;
b. eliminate all forms of violence, discrimination and exploitation against women and children;
c. protect women and children from acts of violence and discrimination in obtaining their constitutionally legitimate rights
d. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children; e. provide services and protection to women and children victims of acts of violence and discrimination, reporters, and witnesses; and
f. facilitate and mediate household disputes to realize the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGELANG REGENCY NUMBER 2 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 18

Paragraph (1)

Cooperation is carried out in the form of, among others, exchange and information, rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence, repatriation and social reintegration as well as cooperation in the field of prevention, handling and recovery of women and children victims of violence and discrimination

Paragraph (2)

Sufficiently clear.

Article 24

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from violence and discrimination.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V

SERVICES FOR VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION Article 7

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to provide services for women and children victims of acts of violence and discrimination.

(2) Services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to witnesses and/or victims of violence and discrimination.

(3) In the context of services as referred to in paragraph (1), a Service Standard Operating Procedure shall be prepared.

Article 20

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance on the implementation of protection of women and children from violence and discrimination.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;

b. technical guidance and training;

c. monitoring; and

d. evaluation.

(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women empowerment and child protection.

Article 13

The obligation of the family as referred to in Article 10 letter d has full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination and to protect women and children as family members.

Article 14

(1) In the framework of services for women and children victims of violence and discrimination as referred to in Article 7, the Regional Government establishes an Institution named Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) or similar institution that has the same function and role as a service center in the protection of women and children from violence and discrimination.

(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as:

a. information center for women and children;

b. service center for women and children victims of violence; and

c. empowerment center for women and children.

(3) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is located in the Region and Sub-district.

(4) In the framework of protection services for women and children from violence at the village level, an Integrated Service Center is established.

(5) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure and working procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct supervision on the implementation of protection of women and children from violence and discrimination.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

Article 25

Laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children from violence and discrimination shall remain in force as long as they are not contradictory to and/or have not been replaced based on this Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Magelang Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.

4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Governmental Affairs that are the authority of the Region.

6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

7. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of physical and verbal means that poses a danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.

11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.

12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 13. Victims of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic losses, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including victims are their heirs.

14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.

15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for trafficking in persons in

Magelang Regency.

16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.

17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the work environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.

19. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and socially.

20. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.

21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

23. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 14

(3) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is located in the Region and Sub-district.

(4) In the framework of protection services for women and children from violence at the village level, an Integrated Service Center is established.

(5) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure and working procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The objectives of protecting women and children from acts of violence and discrimination are to:

a. prevent acts of violence and discrimination against women and children including trafficking in persons;
b. eliminate all forms of violence, discrimination and exploitation against women and children;
c. protect women and children from acts of violence and discrimination in obtaining their constitutionally legitimate rights
d. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children; e. provide services and protection to women and children victims of acts of violence and discrimination, reporters, and witnesses; and
f. facilitate and mediate household disputes to realize the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGELANG REGENCY NUMBER 2 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGELANG REGENCY NUMBER 2 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.

4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Governmental Affairs that are the authority of the Region.

6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

7. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of physical and verbal means that poses a danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.

11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.

12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 13. Victims of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic losses, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including victims are their heirs.

14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.

15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for trafficking in persons in

Magelang Regency.

16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.

17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the work environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.

19. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and socially.

20. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.

21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

23. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Magelang Regency.

7. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of physical and verbal means that poses a danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

10. 11. 12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 13. Victims of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic losses, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including victims are their heirs.

of Pancasila).

Letter b

The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there is no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

The principle of victim protection, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by the family, community and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in the laws and regulations.

The principle of Empowerment is that every effort to protect women and children victims of violence must be oriented towards efforts to strengthen victims both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

The principle of integration means that a series of activities to provide protection to Women and children victims of violence will be carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their position as being vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of such regulation is felt to be not yet able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to the problem of such legislation, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on such thinking, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination is needed that is able to answer as well as provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Responsibilities of the Government to the Participation of the Government, Community and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, the regulation concerning adequate funding sourced from

the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are non-binding is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection of women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.
